q: What do we know about feat-nps-fee-shock-v2 in the nps-drivers project?
a: Fee shock v2 is fees in the 30 days before the send date relative to the prior three-month average, with charges after send date excluded. It replaces v1, which leaked post-send fees. On holdout-2025q4 it adds +0.03 Spearman (0.46 to 0.49, exp-405, 2026-02-05).

q: What came of exp-404 in the nps-drivers project?
a: exp-404 (2026-01-13) showed fee shock v1 lifting holdout-2025q4 Spearman to 0.52, but only 0.44 on the 2026Q1 wave, because the current-month fees included charges after the survey. That produced fnd-nps-fee-top, which fnd-nps-fee-corrected superseded, and led to feat-nps-fee-shock-v2.

q: What does nps-gbm-v2 in the nps-drivers project use?
a: nps-gbm-v2 uses feat-nps-theme-share-v1 (open-text theme shares), feat-nps-txn-freq-v1, feat-nps-complaint-flag-v1 and feat-nps-fee-shock-v2. Behaviour inputs are cut at the send date under dec-nps-no-leak-rule.

q: What is the current NPS driver model in the nps-drivers project?
a: nps-gbm-v2, which supersedes nps-gbm-v1 and was adopted in dec-nps-gbm-v2 on 2026-03-22. It scores Spearman 0.49 on holdout-2025q4 and 0.47 on the 2026Q1 wave.

q: What Spearman does nps-gbm-v2 get on holdout-2025q4 in the nps-drivers project, and what is n?
a: Spearman 0.49 on holdout-2025q4, which has n = 48,210 respondents from the Oct to Dec 2025 wave, measured in exp-405 on 2026-02-05.

q: Why did the nps-drivers project move its driver model to v2?
a: Fee shock v1 used charges from the full current month, so it looked like +0.06 Spearman but fell to 0.44 on the 2026Q1 wave. dec-nps-no-leak-rule (2026-02-12) cut behaviour features at the send date, and nps-gbm-v2 replaced nps-gbm-v1 under dec-nps-gbm-v2 on 2026-03-22.
